toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
What is going on: the doubling is best explained by the tag stock change, not the handler change. Since 1 September, Corvane tags printed at Harlow Bay on Fennick stock fail the airport's automatic tag readers about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% on the old Brackwater stock. Tags from other stations and Pelion tags stay normal on every array, so the readers and the airport system are not the main problem. When counters briefly used Brackwater stock in mid-October, their tags read normally on the same printers. Those extra bags are what get diverted to manual encode and miss their flights. The handler change is not ruled out, because the crew mishandling evidence is anecdotal and unmeasured.

How sure: moderately confident on the tag-stock link, less sure whether the cause is the media itself or its print settings. The manufacturer's bulletin says new media may need different settings.

What to do next: switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater stock now, which is reversible and cheap. Test Fennick stock under controlled print settings and ask Fennick for its conformance data. Hold off on the breach notice and fee withholding. The evidence points away from Tessaly as the main cause, and a notice on this basis would be unfair.
